## Problem

On a phone with a local calendar event but no Google or Microsoft calendar connected, “取消明天的晨会日程” asks for an external calendar connection instead of offering the local event. Changes have the same gap.

Closes #1459.

## Change

- Let the cloud model request a typed local-calendar edit or delete; the phone does not classify the person's text with new keyword or regular-expression rules.
- Require the person to choose and confirm the event, and choose this occurrence or the whole series for a recurring event. Return only a non-sensitive matching receipt to the original task.
- Check permissions, current event identity and provider readback. Reconcile uncertain two-step recurring edits without blindly adding another event.
- Recognize the CalendarKit `recurrenceFrequency: -1` sentinel observed on the real phone as non-recurring.
- Give selectable event rows accessible labels with the event details and selection state.

The [proposed contract and recovery design](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/DigitalMate/blob/4dbc73c7729c03ba137ed7aa0ebe001a0f14807c/docs/architecture/phone-calendar-management-proposal.md) requires owner acceptance before merge. Whole-series edits that move across dates, or change the time when the series already contains exclusions, currently fail closed until recurrence rules can be safely preserved. Local calendar changes do not imply that other attendees were notified.

## Verification so far

- A real JUY-AL50 / OpenHarmony 7.0.0.111 phone ran a temporary diagnostic build with a uniquely created local test calendar. Ordinary edit and delete, recurring single and series delete, recurring single edit, and same-date series edit passed provider readback. The test calendar was removed; existing user events were not modified. This is a CalendarKit owner test, not an end-to-end model-routing verdict.
- HarmonyOS debug HAP compiled successfully; the temporary diagnostic build was replaced with the normal test build.
- After the CI accessibility failure, 38 focused Node tests (including the accessibility gate) and a debug HAP build passed locally.
- 190 Node unit and card tests and 48 selected Python calendar/phone tests passed. WorkSwarm was substituted for the automated integration tests.
- Test-7 v27 runs the verified image built from `bdade257abdc17da6fe66eae77b4af21bbd4da53`, with retained data. The subsequent commit changes only the phone, tests and docs; no server source changed.
- On test-7 v27, the real model requested an edit and then a delete for a uniquely named synthetic event. The phone prefilled the requested 10:00–11:00 time, the edited event was read back at that time, and the deletion produced the device receipt. The test event was removed. The screenshots below show the actual phone UI.
- **Pending:** real-model UI verification of recurring-scope selection; owner/design review and applicable CI. The repeating-event provider operations were exercised on the real phone using the temporary diagnostic build.

## Problem

The Bee-only WorkSwarm launcher uses the fixed `--bee-runtime` argument, while retained factory observation accepted only the Personal Agent launcher. Rotate factory owner PID and revision only for a new Bee generation after the previous child is gone and no prior factory preparation is unknown. Personal Agent defaults are unchanged.

Base `main`, contains integration `694b1b44` (#1471, #1472), lands through `hive/hive2-integration` (#1421).

**Two safeguards for unavailable Bees, kept together at the coordinator's request.** `test_unavailable_factory_does_not_strand_claim_and_recovers` already passes on integration through huben's #1472, which releases an unstarted claim (`release_unstarted_turn`). This PR adds the pre-claim check `BeeHostExecution.ready_for`, wired as `BeeExecutionBridge(ready_turn=...)` through `HiveBeeScheduler` and `Bridge.configure_hive_bee_runtime`. It returns true only when the exact registered Harness and model are ready and the Session's persisted binding equals the registered profile; `commit_runtime_binding` needs no Run, so this can be checked first. When the check fails, the turn is not claimed, which avoids a claim-and-release cycle on every poll. #1472's release still covers a dependency lost between the check and the claim. New test: `test_changed_exact_binding_is_unavailable_before_any_claim`. #1471 (retained factories for the owned Bee runtime) is opt-in groundwork and states it does not address same-version drift. Verified: with #1471 merged onto integration, this test still fails.

## Root cause

The Registry contract says identity bytes describe the actual implementation, and that digests detect drift under the same version. The WorkSwarm Bee Harness registered only the static TOML label `hive-workswarm-bee-harness-v1`. So changed Harness code under version `1` silently resolved an existing Bee Session's persisted binding.

## Fix

`dm_hive_runtime.assembly.bee_runtime.harness_implementation_identity` builds the registered identity from:
- the TOML label;
- a SHA-256 over the source of the methods the registered factory and its lane proxy run for a turn (`ready`, `bind`, `release`, `run`, `open_scoped_session`, `stream_bound_bee`);
- the #1268 `text_run` module those methods call.

Changed code under the same version is a different implementation. A Session bound to the old code resolves as `unavailable` (`MissingDependency`), and #1472 releases the unstarted claim. That Session needs a new incarnation (re-activation) to run on the new code. There is no automatic binding migration. Unchanged code keeps the same identity across restarts; the test now checks this too. The digest does not cover the WorkSwarm adapter transport or the runtime process; the pinned runtime patch hashes cover the runtime.

Operational note: Bee Sessions bound under the old static identity become `unavailable` after this change and need re-activation.

1477.body:
## 背景

#1472（已合入 H2，`b0c120d4`）解决了“工厂不可用时 Bee 认领一直停在 RUNNING”的问题。Codex 审查时提出三个加固点，本 PR 逐一处理。用户已授权（t554「你继续做1472 加固」）。

Refs #1223 #1309 #1316

## 先读代码确认的 Store / Runtime 契约

- **"unavailable" 的来源**：只有 `dm_hive_runtime.assembly.bee_runtime.BeeHostExecution.run_turn` 在进入 Harness 之前的三处返回它：没有精确绑定、实现缺失/未就绪/绑定无效、解析出的不是 `WorkSwarmBeeHarness`。Harness 内部的 `execute_bound_claim` 只会产生 `finished / unresolved / ask_user / confirm / file`，不会产生 `unavailable`。但 #1472 里 bridge 只看字符串，任何注入的 `run_turn` 返回这个字符串都能触发释放，这就是第 1 点的风险。
- **代际围栏**：`_start` 用 `MAX(run_generation)+1` 计算下一个代际，#1472 删除 Run 行后同一代际会被重新分配（run_id 不同）。逐一核对了所有用到 `run_generation` 的地方（hive_busy 的 steer/preempt/queue head/result/run end/answer、hive_store.read_runtime_binding、bee_identity、bee_verifier 的 lane 和 witness、bee_runtime 的 RunOperations key、scheduler 的 answer finisher、question token）：**全部是 (run_id, run_generation) 成对校验，没有只按代际围栏的地方**，所以 #1472 目前不会被利用。但这依赖每个调用方都记得带 run_id，所以本 PR 仍然把代际改成不复用，属于纵深防御。
- **进程内状态**：`BeeHostExecution._evidence`、`WorkSwarmBeeHarness._turns` 都只在内存里，重启就没了，不能作为“从未进入 Harness”的跨重启证据。

## 改动

1. **权威边界：Store 里的持久化进入围栏**（新表 `dm_hive_run_entry_fences`）
   - Bee bridge 走 Host 执行入口时，`claim_next_turn(..., entry_fence=True)` 在同一个事务里写入 `NOT_ENTERED`。
   - `BeeHostExecution.run_turn` 在进入 Harness 前调用 `hive_busy.enter_bee_run`，把状态改成 `ENTERED`；只有提交确认为 True 才进入，返回 False/None（已释放、已结束、提交未知）就不进入。
   - `release_unstarted_turn` 只释放围栏仍为 `NOT_ENTERED` 的 Run。无围栏（旧路径/直接认领）或已 `ENTERED` 的 Run 一律拒绝。
   - bridge 只在收到 Host 执行入口的类型化结果 `HostNotEntered` 时才请求释放；裸字符串 `"unavailable"` 不会触发释放。真正做决定的是 Store 围栏，类型只是请求资格。
   - 释放和进入都在 Store 写锁里串行，两者同时发生时只有一个能成功。
2. **防 ABA**：释放时删除 Run 行（`queue_seq` 唯一约束要求删除），但围栏行改成 `RELEASED` 墓碑并保留 `run_generation`。`_start` 改为取 `dm_hive_runs` 和围栏表的最大代际 +1，所以重新认领的代际严格变大。没有围栏行时，结果和原来的 `MAX+1` 完全一致。
3. **可区分、可观测、可恢复**
   - `BeeRunResult` 新增 `release` 字段：`released` / `refused` / `unknown`。`status` 仍是 `"unavailable"`，G3 SC03-R2 的断言不变。非 `released` 时打 warning 日志。
   - `resume_running`：遇到没有 head 的 RUNNING Run，如果 Store 能证明它没进入过 Harness（`NOT_ENTERED`），就释放它并返回 `idle`，让调度器接着认领同一个任务。这覆盖了释放 ACK 丢失、认领后进入前重启这两种情况。已 `ENTERED` 或无围栏的 Run 仍然 fail closed（`unresolved`，`release=refused`），不会重跑。

4. **与 #1481 Bee Stop 对齐**（Codex 在 6e795402 上的探针：有 Stop 预留时 Bee 仍会进入 Harness；用户 t575 同意在本 PR 修）
   - `enter_bee_run` 在 Run 已有 Stop/preempt 预留时拒绝进入，Harness 不会被启动，因此不存在 Stop 无法中断的运行。
   - 这种 Run 的围栏仍是 `NOT_ENTERED`，没有运行时 Session 可中断，#1481 的 HostBeeStop 会一直停在 STOPPING。新增 `stop_unentered_run`：以围栏作为隔离见证，在同一个提交里把 Run 结束为 `stopped`（Stop 回执随之读作 STOPPED，和中断确认后的效果一致）；如果是 Stop，还会按 `commit_stopped_result` 的同样规则写入任务的 stopped 终态和通知，全有或全无。如果是 preempt，只结束 Run，后继仍由 preempt 的 owner 启动。
   - bridge 在 `run_next` 和 `resume_running`（覆盖丢 ACK 和重启）里调用它，返回 `status=stopped`（preempt 返回 `ended`），`release=stopped`。调度器对 `stopped` 也会发布通知。
   - 已经 `ENTERED` 的 Run 仍完全由 #1481 的 Stop 路径负责（中断确认、record_run_end、commit_stopped_result），本 PR 不改 #1481 的语义和代码。

5. **纵深防御**：H2 新加的 #1484 Bee effect plan 如果指向这个 Run，也会拒绝释放（围栏仍是主要证据）。

不变的部分：Phase 1 行为、Beebou 路径、不带 `entry_fence` 的认领，以及问答栈（#1474 / #1388–#1403，已交给 Jianyu010）都没动；hive_bee_questions/answer 相关代码、selection.py、revival.py、hive_beebou_tools.py、test_phase2_bee_revive.py、test_phase2_workswarm_memory.py、test_phase2_bee_verifier.py 都没改。没有新增 env var，也不需要新配置。

## 测试

- `agent_bridge/tests/test_hive_bee_unavailable_release.py`（真实临时 SQLite Store）：已进入不能释放；无围栏不能释放；已释放不能再进入；伪造 host 被拒；进入和释放并发时只有一个成功；墓碑保留代际，下一次认领代际严格变大。
- 新增 `tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase2_bee_unstarted_recovery.py`（真实 Store、Registry、Host 执行入口、WorkSwarm adapter 和 bridge，只控制 wire 和 ready）：
  - 权威：工厂未就绪时按围栏释放，之后只执行一次；裸字符串不释放；Host 已进入后再返回类型化结果也不释放，并且对账时 fail closed。
  - ABA：两次释放后代际严格递增；针对旧 (run_id, gen) 的 enter / record_run_end / steer 都被拒或 TARGET_STALE；任务只跑一次。
  - 丢 ACK（已提交）：`release=unknown`，下一轮直接认领，只执行一次。
  - 丢 ACK（未提交）：`release=unknown`，Run 仍是 NOT_ENTERED，`resume_running` 按围栏释放后只执行一次。
  - 重启（重新打开 SQLite）：认领后进入前崩溃，重启后按持久证据释放并只执行一次；进入后崩溃或无围栏，重启后 fail closed，不重跑。
  - 并发 Stop：Stop 预留先到，释放被拒，Run 留给 Stop 路径结束（STOPPED）；Stop 结束先到，释放被拒；释放后迟到的 Stop 得到 TARGET_STALE（保留草稿），任务只跑一次。

- Stop 相关（#1481 真实 HostBeeStop 和 Store）：Stop 落在认领和进入之间时不进入、只结算一次，用户重试同一个 Stop 回放 STOPPED 和同一个终态；Stop 落在进入之后时，围栏不结算、不释放、也不允许再进入，由 Stop 路径结束；进入的 ACK 丢失且有 Stop 待处理时只结算一次；结算 ACK 丢失（已提交时已经完整，未提交时下一轮对账结算）；Stop 待处理时重启，按持久证据结算一次，重试 Stop 得到 STOPPED。把 `enter_bee_run` 的预留检查去掉后，有 5 个用例会失败，说明这个修复确实在起作用。

## 门禁（与同一 H2 基线对比）

基线 = H2 `2ae76c35`，PR = `41bc8b8e`（已合入同一 H2）。两边都用仓库内的 WorkSwarm（`harness/personal-agent/deploy/install_runtime.py` 安装 `harness/workswarm`）。

| 门禁 | 基线 H2 2ae76c35 | PR 41bc8b8e |
|---|---|---|
| 架构 Py3.13 全量 | 236 OK | 236 OK |
| bridge（hive/workswarm/memory） | 364 passed, 13 skipped, 7 xfailed | 370 passed, 13 skipped, 7 xfailed（+6 新用例） |
| induced | 8 passed, 7 xfailed | 8 passed, 7 xfailed |
| scenarios/hive | 192 passed, 19 skipped | 210 passed, 19 skipped（+18 新用例） |
| test_hive_runner + admission | 30 passed | 30 passed |
| temp/*（beebou 142, composio-mail 92, connection-foundation 69, feishu 4, hive-beebou 12, hive-runtime 54, hive-worker 99, report-goals 38） | 全过 | 全过，数字相同 |
| temp/hive-memory | 1 个收集错误（PYTHONPATH 找不到 test_hive_worker_workswarm，基线已有） | 相同 |
| temp/mail-signal-pipeline | 2 个收集错误（基线已有） | 相同 |
| check.py（3.12 / 3.13） | rc=0 / rc=0 | rc=0 / rc=0 |
| G3 `--source wheel` | PASS 16, FAIL 0, BLOCKED 1（SC02-R1） | PASS 16, FAIL 0, BLOCKED 1（SC02-R1），逐项一致 |

没有新增失败。说明：上一轮（`7ee21f98`）G3 有一次 SC02-B1 的 owner test 在关停时超时（Bridge shutdown deadline）。我在同一份 package-proof 上单独重跑了该用例两次，都通过；整轮 G3 重跑也全过，判断为负载下的偶发问题。本轮 `41bc8b8e` 的 G3 一次通过。

## 仍未覆盖的边界

- 进入围栏只能证明“没有进入 Harness”。Host 已进入 Harness 但在写 head 前崩溃的 Run，仍然要靠 owner 对账（fail closed），本 PR 没有自动恢复它。
- `enter_bee_run` 提交结果未知时 Host 不进入，但围栏可能已经是 ENTERED。这种 Run 会 fail closed 留给对账，属于有意的保守选择。
- `enter_bee_run` 已经提交为 ENTERED（包括 ACK 丢失但实际已提交的情况）、但 Harness 还没打开运行时 Session 时到达的 Stop，按 #1481 的语义停在 STOPPING，要等 Session 打开后用户重试 Stop 才能确认。本 PR 没有改变这一点。
- 围栏/墓碑行目前不清理，每个 Bee Run 一行。保留期策略需要另定。
- 本 PR 之前已经存在、没有围栏行的 RUNNING Run，不会被自动释放（无证据），仍然 fail closed。

## Why

The SC05-M5 handover test `test_sc05_m5_ingestion_after_revival_keeps_the_migration_queryable` reactivated the evicted Bee under its original `bee_id`. That is H-D2 revival. The product owner replaced it with scheme two on 2026-11-14 (#1268 comment 6873130205, #1228 decision register): an evicted `bee_id` is never reactivated.

`hive/hive2-integration` (#1450) defaults `retire_evicted_identity` to true, and there the test fails with `(1, ARCHIVED) != (2, ACTIVE)`. On main it still passes, because main's default is still false.

## What

- **Handover test** (`temp/hive-memory/tests/test_hive_memory_handover.py`): `test_sc05_m5_ingestion_after_eviction_keeps_the_migration_queryable` now follows scheme two.
  - After the eviction, a new `bee_id` takes the slot.
  - The new Bee starts from the old Profile reference, gets its own Session and starts with an empty, separate Local Memory.
  - The old generation's sealed migration is ingested late: first the provider is unavailable, then it ACKs, then it publishes once.
  - The migration stays queryable by its `migration_id`. The new Bee's Local Memory is untouched.
  - The test never touches the evicted ID again, so it holds whichever way `retire_evicted_identity` is set. It does not guard the scheme-two rule itself; the guards are listed under the merge plan below.
- **Provider test** (`test_hive_memory_provider.py`): renamed to `test_ingestion_after_eviction_stays_queryable_by_the_original_id`. Its behaviour is unchanged.

## Summary

Producer `bee_stop` (#1309) for G3 row **SC02-R2**: "Stop request receipt, terminal, execution-right isolation and physical release are each queryable; capacity stays held until release." This is the coordinator-approved design (option A, Store half in this PR); the preempt workaround is not used. Branched from `hive/hive2-integration` `37e0c5e3`, which contains main and #1416; base `main`; lands through `hive/hive2-integration` (#1421).

> **#1311 Store schema change (E/C extension) — for the HIVE1 owner (Jianyu010) to review.**
> - `dm_hive_controls.intent` CHECK gains `'stop'`.
> - New table `dm_hive_stopped_results(workspace_id, principal_id, task_ref, run_id, run_generation, stop_operation_id, stopped_at_ms)`, with PK `(workspace_id, principal_id, task_ref)` and UNIQUE `(workspace_id, principal_id, run_id)`.
> - New `HiveBusyControls` operations: `stop`, `commit_stopped_result`, `read_stopped_result`. `start_successor` now only starts a preempt's successor; for a Stop it returns the receipt.
> - **Migration.** Fresh workspaces get the new CHECK from `BUSY_SCHEMA`. For an existing workspace, `HiveBusyControls.__init__` runs `_migrate_controls_stop_intent` in one Store transaction: it creates `dm_hive_controls_stop_rebuild` with the new CHECK, copies every row column-for-column, drops the old table and renames. It is skipped when the table already admits `'stop'` (reopen is a no-op). A crash rolls the whole rebuild back and the next open repeats it. The migration stays inside the hive-busy owner (no new export), so the trusted module inventory is unchanged.

## Flow (each step separately queryable)

1. **Receipt.** `hive.bee.stop {operation_id, task_ref}` on the full-user WebSocket calls `HostBeeStop.stop`, which calls `hive_busy.stop`.
   - The new `stop` control has no successor and returns STOPPING.
   - It holds the Run's single reservation, which closes steer, answers, queued supplements, `save_queue_head`, a late natural `commit_text_result` and #1472's `release_unstarted_turn`.
   - Replay is keyed by the task, so a repeated operation ID returns the original receipt. A different task under the same ID is CONFLICT; a second Stop on the same Run is CONFLICT. With no RUNNING Run the receipt is TARGET_STALE.
2. **Stop and execution-right isolation.** The Host interrupts the exact runtime Session that its own `BeeHostExecution` opened for the claimed Run. The Harness now records it per Run, bounded by `retained_runs`.
   - The interrupt is `WorkSwarmAdapter.abort`, i.e. `chat.interrupt` plus the `chat.interrupt_result` confirmation from #1469, bounded by `[stop] confirm_timeout_ms`.
   - Only a confirmed result is the stop witness (`hive-bee-stop-v1:<sha256>`). The Host then calls `record_run_end(..., "stopped", isolation_witness=...)` and the receipt reads STOPPED.
   - **Unconfirmed** (timeout, refusal, disconnect, or no Session this Host opened, e.g. after a restart): STOPPING, or AWAITING_STOP_CONFIRMATION for an end without a witness. There is then no terminal, no notice and no slot release; a later call with the same operation ID retries.
3. **Terminal.** `commit_stopped_result` marks the task `cancelled` (the existing task-state terminal; `stopped` would need a second table rebuild of `dm_hive_tasks`). It writes `dm_hive_stopped_results` and the notice in one commit.
   - The SC03-D2 publisher (`HiveResultPublisher`, plus `hive.result.get`) now delivers either terminal kind. A stopped notice is `digitalmate.task.text` with `state: "stopped"`, `final: true` and no result text; the completed-text frame is unchanged.
4. **Physical release.** After the terminal, the Bridge runs the #1439 `HiveSlotRelease` pass. The ended, witnessed Run no longer holds execution, and the slot is handed over only by that pass's own release witness. Capacity is held until then.

Tunables are in `dm_hive_runtime/config/bee_runtime.toml` `[stop]` (`confirm_timeout_ms`, `witness_prefix`). All SQL is plain literals.

**Limits.** The client has no task listing, so it learns a Bee's `task_ref` from the Store or a notice. The tests read it from the Store, as the QA runner does. The witness relies on WorkSwarm's interrupt confirmation in the ask-only owned runtime, same as the completion witness.

## Files

- Store: `session_proximity/hive_busy.py`.
- Host: `temp/hive-runtime/.../assembly/bee_stop.py` (new) and `bee_runtime.py` (per-Run lane Session, `live_session`).
- Config: `config/settings.py` and `bee_runtime.toml`.
- Gateway and wiring: `server_engine/server.py` (`_install_hive_bee_stop`, only the Bee-runtime lines), `hive_bee_runtime.py` (`stopper`), and `hive_bee_execution.py` (stopped frame in the publisher and result read).
- Registration and docs: `temp/hive-runtime/ownership.json`, `README.md`, `bee-runtime-observation.md`.

There are two trivial conflicts:

## Summary

This builds the producer `bee_effect_steps` (#1309) so that G3's **SC02-R1** can run through the product. It lands through `hive/hive2-integration` (cut from `e475805b`, merged with integration `8fe0f98e`, which includes #1481 Bee Stop, #1473 and #1424). The base stays `main`.

The owned Bee WorkSwarm runtime from #1442 is still **ask-only by default**. Effects mode is opt-in:

- CLI: `engine_cli serve --hive-results --hive-beebou-id <id> --hive-turns --hive-bees --hive-bee-effects`
- Assembly: `configured_bridge(..., hive_bees=True, hive_bee_effects=True)`
- Config: `dm_hive_runtime/config/bee_effects.toml`. `[mode] default = "ask_only"`; the allowlist and the gate limits are tunables there.

In effects mode, the Host-owned tool rail from #1409 (`host_ask_only_rail` in `deploy/runtime_patches/session_unload.py`) still refuses every tool except `ask_user` and the allowlisted tool `mcp_hive-bee-effects_ledger_record`. The runtime never executes that tool itself. The rail hands each call to the **Host effect gate** (`dm_hive_runtime.assembly.bee_effects.BeeEffectGate`) over a private Unix socket that needs a token. Each call goes through two steps:

1. **Admission** (`before_tool_call`)
   - The gate resolves the Run that the Host bound to this runtime Session for the current turn (`BeeHostExecution.run_turn` → `bind_lane`).
   - It re-reads the Session's persisted exact binding while that claim's Run is RUNNING. The Store also re-checks the Run, its generation, the queue item and preempt.
   - If a steer was accepted first, the call is **HELD**. "Accepted first" means the steer is in flight from the Host, or the runtime reports pending steering for the next step. The model then decides again with the supplement.
   - The decision is persisted in the Store before any effect, as PLANNED, HELD or REFUSED, under `bee-effect:<run>:<generation>:<call>`.
2. **Execution** (`after_tool_call`)
   - This runs inside the call's own execution window, while WorkSwarm still counts the tool as running, so a steer that arrives now is admitted into the *next* step.
   - The PLANNED plan runs once, with the operation ID as idempotency key, and then settles as EXECUTED.

**Unknown outcomes.** An exception, a lost reply or a crash leaves the plan PLANNED. It is reconciled by operation ID through the provider's `lookup`: when a finished turn is released, and at startup. It settles as EXECUTED or NOT_EXECUTED and is **never executed again**. A replayed call returns the stored decision.

**Steer.** `BeeEffectGate.steer` calls Store `HiveBusyControls.steer` (PENDING_APPLY) and then delivers the steer to the running step.
- The WorkSwarm Gateway acknowledges a steer before the runtime decides on it. So the Host waits for the runtime's own `chat.input_received` witness, using the new `WorkSwarmAdapter.steer_witnessed`.
- The steer counts as APPLIED only on the `chat.output_phase` whose `applied_input_ids` names it. That phase is the witness passed to `record_steer_applied`.
- If the runtime refuses the steer (for example between steps), it stays accepted only, and the Store reports it UNKNOWN when the Run ends.
- Beebou's `dispatch(mode=steer)` follow-up uses the same gate in effects mode (`HiveBeebouTools(steer=...)`). Note that Beebou's default follow-up mode is still `queue`.

**Substitute.** The only provider is the labelled **SUBSTITUTE controlled ledger** (`SubstituteLedger`): a durable ledger keyed by operation ID, so tests can count executions. `server_engine/hive_bee_effect_mcp.py` only lists the allowlist to the Bee model. Effects mode turns off progressive tool search, which would hide MCP tools behind `tool_search`/`tool_call`, and the rail refuses those.

### SC02-R1 branches covered

| R1 branch | Where |
|---|---|
| A Bee step proposes an external effect (tool advertised to the model) | `test_phase2_cli_bee_effects` (all three) |
| Supplement submitted **while sampling**: the old sample's effect is HELD, the model decides again with the supplement, the new call runs once, and the steer is APPLIED on the runtime phase witness | `test_supplement_while_sampling_holds_the_old_effect_and_the_new_decision_runs_once` |
| Supplement **after the step is sealed**, while a call is already executing: that call settles once under its original operation ID, the supplement applies at the next step, a non-allowlisted tool is refused by the rail, a policy refusal is persisted as REFUSED, and a forged or stale request is refused | `test_supplement_after_the_step_is_sealed_lets_executing_calls_settle_once_and_refusals_hold` |
| Crash or restart between plan and result: reconciled as EXECUTED, never re-executed | `test_restart_between_plan_and_result_reconciles_without_executing_again` |
| Lost result, admitted but never executed, and replay | `temp/hive-runtime/tests/test_bee_effects.py` |

### Producer row for HIVE2 QA (`tests/scenarios/hive/producers.toml`)

```toml
[roles.bee_effect_steps]
owner = "1309"
title = "A Bee step that can propose external effects through the Host effect gate (opt-in --hive-bee-effects; SUBSTITUTE controlled ledger), with steer ordered against effect admission"
module = "dm_hive_runtime.assembly.bee_effects"
attrs = ["BeeEffectGate.decide", "BeeEffectGate.steer", "BeeEffectGate.reconcile", "BeeEffectGate.bind_lane", "BeeEffectGate.release_lane"]

```

QA reaches the gate as `bridge.hive_bee_runtime.effects.gate`, its socket as `bridge.hive_bee_runtime.effects`, and the Store rows in `dm_hive_bee_effect_plans`. The ledger is at `<workspace>/hive-bee-effects/ledger.jsonl`.

### HIVE1-owned code touched (flagged)

- **#1311 Store** (`session_proximity/hive_busy.py`): this adds `dm_hive_bee_effect_plans` to `BUSY_SCHEMA`, plus `HiveBusyControls.record_bee_effect`, `settle_bee_effect`, `read_bee_effects` and `_bee_effect`. The changes are additive; steer, Run end and the other controls are unchanged. Effect plans are Store state, per `temp/AGENTS.md`, so they sit next to the Beebou tool plans. Admission requires `_queue_run_matches`, so a preempt reservation closes effect admission.

- Also flagged: the #1409 rail (`session_unload.py`) is copied into the runtime wheel, so the pinned runtime must be rebuilt with `install_runtime.py`. With `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_BEE_EFFECTS` unset, the rail behaves exactly as before.

> **Hive Phase 3 constituent (Step 3.4, #1312). Do not merge to `main` directly.** It lands through `hive/hive3-integration` with the other Phase 3 constituents, in one merge-commit PR.

## Why

The SC05-M1 evidence on main runs on a library the same test wrote seconds earlier, not a copy. That library is tiny (2 turns, one batch). Its structured memory covers only `preference` and `profile`, and the records were written with `MemoryStore.put`, which skips the proposal path. SC05-M2's high water and cutoff were checked only on the `ScriptedHistory` substitute. #1312 asks for a real old database copy with history, existing structured memory, pending questions and committed receipts, written by the owners' writers. The full gap review is on #1312.

## What

- **Old library fixture** (`temp/hive-memory/tests/hive_memory_old_library.py`, sized by `hive_memory_old_library.toml`).
  - The pre-upgrade Bridge writes the library in-process through its own entry, `Bridge.dispatch` with `digitalmate.request` frames:
    - 20 completed Home turns (`task.create` with `submission_id`, `run=True`).
    - 1 question answered before the upgrade (`task.answer`).
    - 1 pending ask_user question.
    - The receipts of all 22 turns, each read back by a retry that must answer the same task as a duplicate.
  - One memory record per legacy kind `need/profile/preference/fact/query` goes through `MemoryStore.apply` (the proposal path) and then the review decision. That includes a correction chain, a rejected record and a pending record.
  - No hand-written SQL and no direct table writes.
  - Tests open **copies** only (`OldLibrary.copy_to`). The original's SHA-256 digest is checked after every test.
  - Measured size: 15 files, about 1.2 MB, 27 backfill keys (4 batches). It builds in about 3.6 s.
  - `python3 hive_memory_old_library.py --out DIR [--plan FILE]` writes a durable copy for a soak.
- **Owner tests** (`temp/hive-memory/tests/test_hive_memory_old_library.py`, 10 tests):
  - **SC05-M1**
    - On the copy: every old task view and room message opens as the old client saw it, and every receipt answers its submission.
    - The pending card is the same.
    - A new message completes before backfill advances.
    - The candidate runs only the new message.
    - Backfill registers every finished turn and every approved memory under its candidate class (`legacy_kinds`). Superseded, rejected and pending records are never registered; the pending question is deferred as in flight.
    - The production registry registers fragments only, with no class.
  - **SC05-M2** on the real legacy store:
    - The high water is fixed once and kept across a candidate restart.
    - With the cutoff placed exactly on a real turn, that turn is included and later turns and memories are left out.
    - A new turn, a new memory and a correction written after the cutoff are not registered.
    - Batch by batch, `remaining` drops by the batch's members, and every unit is held under its original key: `ACCEPTED`, then `PUBLISHED`.
  - **Ops**: rate-limit spacing, the model budget across batches and a restart, pause and resume, the progress query.
- **Backfill Ops keys** (`config/backfill.toml`, read by `BackfillSettings` and `BackfillRunner`):
  - `pace.min_batch_interval_s` (rate limit between batch starts per scope).
  - `budget.judge_calls_per_run` (judge calls per backfill identity, counted from `hb_items`, so restarts count).
  - `BackfillProgress.judged`.
  - Defaults (0.2 s, 200) are unmeasured starting points for Runtime / Ops.

Substitutes are labelled where they are built:
- `ScriptedBackend` (CONTROLLED model runtime in both Bridges).
- `ExecutionLog` (wraps `EngineService.execute`, never replaces it).
- `ScriptedJudge` (budget test only).
- `MemoryStore.put` standing in for the person's review decision (main has no review RPC).

NOT_RUN: a library written by v0.1.10 writers, and the Mobile Gateway process. SC05-M2's live relay stays **BLOCKED** (`live_ingestion`: the Store owner's durable-cursor contract is unsigned). The new tests prove only that backfill leaves post-cutoff writes alone.

Finding, pinned by a test: a correction approved after the cutoff makes the old original `superseded`, so backfill skips it, and the successor belongs to the live path. Until live ingestion exists, neither text reaches Global Memory.

1491.body:
## Problem

In huben0423-hw's combined H2 run (a6e22ae9, reported on #1223 and #1311), two Bees finished their WorkSwarm work: Run `ENDED`, task `completed`, Host completion witness recorded. Their `dm_hive_inputs.consumed_at_ms` stayed NULL. `HiveStore._idle()` refuses any Bee with an unconsumed input, so with every slot full a new Bee got `CAPACITY_BUSY`.

Cause: nothing on the Bee path consumes a Bee input. Beebou consumes its inputs inside `commit_beebou_context`, but no Bee commit did the same. (Queued supplements were already consumed in `settle_queued_supplement`.) G3's eviction rows (SC02-R3, SC03-B8) only evict Bees that never got work, which is why they missed it. The same leak also used up the per-Bee `bee_new_tasks` admission quota.

## Owner decision (#1311, final)

**A Bee input is consumed only after that turn's Bee context is durably committed to the Session Store; Host witnesses alone are insufficient. Supersedes the earlier 'accept, split Stop' note.** Design discussion: issuecomment-6880887042.

## Fix: consume only against a committed Session Store context record

**Record: `dm_hive_bee_contexts`** (Store-owned, `BUSY_SCHEMA`).
- One row per committed Bee turn, keyed by `(run_id, turn)`. `turn` is `run`, `queue:<seq>`, `answer:<op>` or `stop:<op>`.
- It holds the HostAPI `ContextSnapshot` and its sha256, plus a per-Session revision.
- `context_ref` is the authoritative witness and becomes `consume_witness`.

**Write: `hive_busy.commit_bee_context`**, generation-fenced and idempotent by the original IDs.
- **Refused:** another task's Run, a stale run or Session generation (the intake must be open), a `completed` context for a Run that is not RUNNING, and a `stopped` context without its confirmed Stop.
- **Replay:** returns the same `context_ref`; a different snapshot is refused.

**Writers** (the snapshot is no longer discarded):
- `BeeHostExecution.run_turn`: the completed snapshot, after its lane releases, so the steers it applied are covered.
- `BeeAnswerResume.resume`: `answer:<op>`.
- `HostBeeStop`: the snapshot as of the stop (the admitted input), before the stopped terminal.
- An unknown outcome is retried once with the same IDs; if still unknown, nothing is consumed and the Bee stays busy.

**Consumption** happens in whichever Store transaction commits second, so it is a fenced, recoverable handoff:

| Input | Needs | `consume_witness` / `consume_kind` |
|---|---|---|
| Task `new` input | Text or stopped terminal **and** a context record of the Run | The Run's first `context_ref` / `context` |
| Queued supplement | Settlement **and** the `queue:<seq>` record | That `context_ref` / `context` |
| Immediate steer | APPLIED **and** a later context record of the Run (`record_steer_applied` alone no longer consumes) | That `context_ref` / `context` |
| Never-entered stopped Run (#1477) | Entry fence `NOT_ENTERED` and Run ended `stopped` (`stop_unentered_run`); there is no Bee context | The `hive-not-entered:` fence witness / `settled` |

**Unchanged and recovery:**
- `reconcile_terminal_inputs` consumes only where the terminal and a record (or the never-entered fence) exist. There is no pre-fix repair.
- `_idle()` and the admission quotas are unchanged.
- `consume_kind` (CHECK `context`|`settled`) is added to existing workspaces once, when `HiveBusyControls` opens.

### Please review: #1311 Store changes (owner: Jianyu010)

All in `session_proximity/hive_busy.py`, and `hive_store.py` gains the `consume_kind` column:
- New: `dm_hive_bee_contexts`, `commit_bee_context`, `read_bee_contexts`, `read_run`.
- Changed: the consumption helpers, `settle_queued_supplement`, `commit_text_result` / `commit_stopped_result` (consume against the record), `record_steer_applied` (no longer consumes) and `reconcile_terminal_inputs`.
- The Host side (`temp/hive-runtime`) changes `bee_runtime.py`, `bee_answer.py` and `bee_stop.py`.

## Tests

- **`agent_bridge/tests/test_hive_bee_input_consumption.py`** (15 Store tests):
  - a terminal with Host witnesses only consumes nothing;
  - context then terminal, terminal then context;
  - a crash between the context commit and consumption recovers (child exits after the commit);
  - a lost terminal ACK;
  - fences: stale run generation, another task, a closed Session generation, a non-RUNNING Run, a bad digest, the host;
  - replay idempotence;
  - Stop: context as of the stop before and after the stopped terminal, and before the confirmed interrupt;
  - the never-entered Stop is settled by its fence;
  - steers (APPLIED alone is not enough; UNAPPLIED and UNKNOWN never consumed);
  - the queued supplement's own turn record;
  - the answer continuation;
  - the recovery pass;
  - the `consume_kind` migration.
- **`tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase2_bee_verifier.py`:** the real `run_turn` over a controlled wire commits the `run` record, and the input is consumed against it.
- **`test_phase2_bee_stop.py`:** the real `HostBeeStop` commits `stop:<op>` before the stopped terminal; replay keeps one record.
- **`tests/scenarios/hive/test_phase2_cli_bee_worked_eviction.py`:** the real owned-WorkSwarm journey (two Bees work; worked A evicted after its real `session.unload` witness; B untouched through a lost ACK; retired A takes no work; restart recovery). It now asserts `consume_witness` is the Run's `bee-context:` record.

## Gates (head 206c6da8, on integration 0d7eb6aa)

- `tools/architecture/check.py`: 0 findings, ownership policy unchanged. `tests/architecture/test_domains.py`: 35 passed.
- Store and Bridge Hive suites: 140 passed. Bridge `test_hive_*`, `test_workswarm_*` and `test_session_proximity_hive_*`: 378 passed; the 8 failures are the known `test_workswarm_runtime_phase`.
- `tests/scenarios/hive -k test_phase2`: 211 passed, 19 skipped (runtime off).
- `temp/*/tests`: all pass.
- `tests/architecture`: 236 passed.
- **Real-runtime** (pinned runtime, checkout): the worked-eviction, Stop and question journeys give 4 passed. `run_hive` SC02-R3 gives **PASS** (`inputs_consumed: 0 of 1 still unconsumed`).

## Open items (not changed here)

- **Immediate-mode steers have no producer.** Beebou's default `followup = "queue"` goes through queued supplements, which are consumed. If a deployment sets `followup = "steer"`, those `dm_hive_inputs` rows have no production caller of `BeeEffectGate.steer` / `hive_busy.steer`, so they stay unconsumed and keep that Bee non-evictable (fail closed). Delivery should route them with `operation_id = message_id`, which is the link `record_steer_applied` now uses.
- **`UNAPPLIED` steers are never consumed.** An `UNAPPLIED` steer was proven never part of the context, so it is not consumed here, and it also keeps the Bee busy forever. The Store owner should decide whether such a row needs a terminal "settled, not in context" state.

- **`dm_hive_runtime.config.deploy`** (new, registered in `temp/hive-runtime/ownership.json` under `hive-runtime-config`) resolves `turns`, `results`, `bees`, `beebou_id` and `bee_effects`. Precedence: explicit argv flag, then `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_*` environment, then a TOML named by `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_CONFIG`, then the packaged `hive_deploy.toml`. **Every packaged default is off**, so an unconfigured server passes no Hive option to `serve`, as before.
- **`engine_cli`**: the Hive booleans are tri-state (`--hive-x` / `--no-hive-x`, default unset), so explicit argv still overrides in both directions. The #1500 option dependencies (Beebou ID and turns need results; Bees need turns; effects need Bees) are checked on the effective values; a refusal names the source and stops before `serve`. Hive options on a non-serve command are refused.
- **Product Beebou ID**: with turns on and no Beebou ID from argv, env or deploy TOML, serve uses `dm_hive_beebou` `identity.toml` (#1494, as in #1500), and the startup log shows its source as `identity`. An explicit `--hive-beebou-id`, `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_BEEBOU_ID` or TOML `beebou_id` overrides it. `--hive-bees` / `DIGITALMATE_HIVE_BEES` no longer need an explicit ID.
- **Bee effects** selected by the environment or a TOML file also need `[hive] bee_effects_allow`, which only a TOML file can set and which must equal `bee_effects.toml`'s `[[tools]]` names, so a grown runtime allowlist needs re-approval. `--hive-bee-effects` on argv keeps its existing operator opt-in.
- **Startup log**: one JSON line on **stderr**, `{"event": "hive_settings", "turns": {"value": …, "source": "argv|env|config|default"}, …, "config": <path|null>}`. stdout keeps the `listening` handshake that harnesses read as the first line.
- **Example**: `harness/personal-agent/deploy/hive-deploy.example.toml` (env and TOML forms). README section in `temp/hive-runtime/README.md`. The runbook (#1492) documents the ADX template env.

**Composes with #1494 / #1500:** this only *selects* options. #1500's `resolve_hive_result_authorizer` (direct token or gateway, never both) still decides whether results may start; it is untouched here.

## Verification (local, Python 3.13, head `69ce4017`)

- `temp/hive-runtime/tests` (incl. `test_hive_deploy_settings.py`: mapping, spellings, blank ID, TOML and precedence, malformed/unknown/unreadable TOML, #1500 dependency refusals with source, Bees without an explicit ID, `with_beebou_id`, effects allowlist): 66 passed, 45 subtests.
- Bridge `tests/test_hive_serve_settings.py`, `test_hive_serve_injection.py`, `test_hive_result_gateway_startup.py`, `test_configured_context.py`: 40 passed, 19 subtests (identity.toml fallback and its log source, argv override of it, env reaches serve, `--no-` override, example).
- Architecture: `tools/architecture/check.py --policy docs/implementations/migration/module-ownership.json`: **0 findings**.
- `tests/test_entry_point.py`: 4 failures (occupied port, SIGTERM with stdin open, stdin EOF, real scripted bridge). These are a **main baseline failure on this Mac**: identical on the unchanged base `fdf959b6c`, and reproduced by the Phase 2 coordinator on main `83e4e9cd`. CI does not run them (server-ut-st is skipped on PRs). The server-ut-st Docker sandbox result for this branch and for main `83e4e9cd` will follow, to separate the local environment from a real failure.

Not run yet: the full isolated server suite (`server-ut-st` LOCAL_REQUIRED, local sandbox), which waits for the HIVE2 QA quiet period to end, and a deployed test env showing the effective flags.

> **Hive Phase 3 constituent (behaviour QA lane, #1244 SC04-E2/E3, #1316 Step 3.3/3.5). Do not merge to `main` directly.** It lands through `hive/hive3-integration` with the other Phase 3 constituents, in one merge-commit PR.
>
> **Stacked on #1295.** The first commit merges #1295's head `d4527903` (the SC04-E1 graders in `tests/eval/hive/*`), because this suite calls those graders. Until #1295 lands, this PR's diff also shows #1295's files. Review only `8b04fc1b`.

## Why

The #1295 graders replay hand-written traces. They cannot tell whether Beebou behaves *reasonably* on a real server with a real model. This lane supplies real multi-turn traces and human-style judgement for:

- mixed topics within one message and across messages;
- whether Beebou answers itself or dispatches, and whether that call is reasonable;
- routing: follow-ups reach the Bee already on the task, a new topic gets a new or reused Bee sensibly, and ambiguity gets a clarifying question;
- eviction. Phase 2 had a real bug here: unconsumed Bee inputs blocked eviction, so slots filled up with `CAPACITY_BUSY`. Scheme two must also hold (an evicted `bee_id` is never revived).

## What

- **Cases.** `tests/eval/hive-live/cases/*.json` holds 44 scripted multi-turn cases (zh 31, en 13). For each turn, a case gives:
  - the user text;
  - the allowed decisions, and the weak ones that score UNREASONABLE;
  - aliases bound to the Bees it creates;
  - routing, eviction, precondition, language and mention signals;
  - a rubric for what code cannot decide.

  A `fill` setup macro fills the slot count the Store actually reports, with idle or busy Bees, so the eviction cases adapt to it (the product default is 4).

  | Category | Cases |
  | --- | --- |
  | Small talk versus a task | 4 |
  | Two topics in one message | 4 |
  | Topic switch and return | 4 |
  | Follow-up to the Bee already working on it | 4 |
  | Similar Bees and ambiguous references | 4 |
  | Steer versus a new task | 4 |
  | Answer directly, dispatch or clarify | 6 |
  | Location and fact corrections | 3 |
  | Capacity, eviction and scheme two | 7 |
  | Chinese and English | 4 |
  | **Total** | **44** |

  The capacity cases are:
  - full with idle Bees, so the LRU idle Bee is evicted and the new Bee gets a new ID (the Phase 2 regression);
  - recently used is not the LRU victim;
  - all busy gives honest `CAPACITY_BUSY`;
  - returning to an evicted Bee's topic gives a new Bee, and the old ID stays only in history;
  - with one idle Bee, only that Bee is evicted;
  - an explicit reference to an evicted Bee's output;
  - no eviction while a slot is free.
- **Driver** (`drive.py`, `livelib/`). It reaches the real entry the way a client does: `hive.message.send` over `/digitalmate/ws` with a bearer token. There are two transports:
  - `local_cli` starts the installed wheel's `engine_cli serve --hive-results --hive-beebou-id beebou --hive-turns --hive-bees` on a fresh workspace for each case repeat;
  - `ws` uses a deployed server's business entry.

  For every turn it records:
  - the Host tool plan (`dm_hive_beebou_tool_plans`: each model call with the Host result);
  - the reply, the reply projection and the pushed frames;
  - timings and waits;
  - read-only Store snapshots before and after: bindings, slots, evictions, retired IDs, activation claims, tasks, deliveries and unconsumed-input counts.

  Overlapping messages (sent while the previous normal turn runs) exercise the quick reply. Tunables are in `tests/eval/config/hive-live.toml`. Secrets come only from `--env-file` and are never written into traces.
- **Grader** (`grade.mjs`, `view.mjs`, `checks.mjs`).
  - Each recorded turn becomes a #1295-format transcript. #1295's checks run on it unchanged: `hive_no_evicted_revival`, `hive_steer_target`, `hive_quick_reply_language` and `hive_no_false_done`. They read `hive-replay.toml` with only `[tools]` replaced by the real names.
  - Live checks cover:
    - decision signatures (`answer` / `clarify` / `capacity_busy` / `new:spawn` / `new:reuse` / `steer`);
    - routing to aliases, `fresh` IDs and distinct Bees for distinct topics;
    - LRU-idle eviction and the victim;
    - `CAPACITY_BUSY` only when every slot is busy, with the idle Bees' unconsumed inputs listed otherwise;
    - slot invariants, scheme two (including Session reuse), false "done" in normal replies, report turns taking no action, language and corrected weather location.
  - Verdict per repeat: FAIL > ERROR > UNREASONABLE > PASS.
    - A failed precondition is a setup ERROR, not a FAIL.
    - Missing evidence is ERROR, never PASS.
    - A human `judgement.json` may keep or lower a code PASS, never raise a verdict or override a code FAIL or ERROR.
- **Docs.** `docs/scenarios/hive-behaviour-qa.md` covers the entry, trace format, checks, verdict rules, commands, limits and the generated case catalogue (a test checks it for drift). The scenario index, UPDATES and test-mapping are updated. `/artifacts/hive-live/` is ignored.

## How to run

```sh
node tests/eval/hive-live/grade.mjs --validate          # 44 cases valid
python3 tests/eval/hive-live/drive.py --plan             # expand cases, no network
# Phase B (real server, real model):
python3 tests/eval/hive-live/drive.py --env-file ENV --python PY --model-label reference --run-id ref-1
python3 tests/eval/hive-live/drive.py --env-file ENV --transport ws --observer sqlite_command --run-id t9-1
node tests/eval/hive-live/grade.mjs --run artifacts/hive-live/ref-1 [--judgement FILE]
```

## Verification (source `8b04fc1b`, this Mac, no real runtime)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `node --test tests/eval/hive-live.test.mjs`: case validation, catalogue drift, and a positive and a negative FIXTURE trace for each live check and for the reused #1295 checks | 15/15 pass |
| `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests/eval/hive-live -p 'test_hive_live_*.py'`: plan expansion, env file, read-only observer, and an end-to-end run of `drive.py` through the real `LocalCli` transport against a FAKE server, graded by `grade.mjs` | 10/10 pass |
| `node --test tests/eval/eval.test.mjs tests/eval/hive-replay.test.mjs tests/eval/hive-sc04.test.mjs tests/eval/hive-live.test.mjs` | 112/112 pass |
| `node tests/eval/run-evals.mjs --validate` | 98/98 task contracts |

FIXTURE traces and the FAKE server prove only the driver and grader contract. They are not product evidence.

**Not run.**
- Every case against a real server and model (Phase B, waiting for the coordinator's go and a Hive-capable environment).
- `local_cli` against the real wheel: it needs the WorkSwarm runtime, and HIVE2 QA owns this Mac until END.
- Whether test-9's entry forwards `hive.message.send`, and how its Store can be read read-only.

## Limits

- Quick-reply and secondary-preparation tool calls never reach the tool plan. "Quick reply makes zero tool calls" stays with SC03-B3. This suite grades only the quick reply's language and false "done".
- The weather cases (3) need a read-only weather tool. They are `NOT_RUN` unless the target declares `readonly:weather` in `[capabilities].granted`.
- Busy setups rely on long tasks. When the model finishes early, that repeat is a setup ERROR to rerun, not a FAIL.
- In `ws` mode cases share the account's roster. The checks use per-turn snapshots, so they stay valid.
- CI enrollment is not done: the Eval workflow runs only `eval.test.mjs`. The rows for that are proposed to the coordinator; no shared gate or runner file is touched.
